claims.explanation: Dofetilide is a potent blocker of the hERG (KCNH2) potassium channel, and its selective antiproliferative effects across cancer cell lines likely reflect dependence on KCNH2/hERG expression or activity for proliferation and survival. Lines with high KCNH2 expression or mutations that drive hERG-dependent signaling (e.g., BRAF, PTEN loss) may be sensitized, while those with low KCNH2 expression or compensatory potassium channel expression are protected. The observed enrichment of BRAF and PTEN mutations in sensitive lines suggests that MAPK/PI3K pathway activation may cooperate with hERG blockade to reduce viability.

features.basis: Dofetilide is a high-affinity hERG (KCNH2) blocker; hERG expression is required for drug sensitivity
BRAF mutations enriched in sensitive melanoma and colorectal lines; MAPK activation may increase hERG dependence
PTEN loss enriched in sensitive lines; PI3K/AKT activation may enhance hERG-dependent survival
Compensatory potassium channel expression may bypass hERG blockade
Alternative inward rectifier potassium channel may maintain viability when hERG is blocked
Background potassium channel expression may reduce dependence on hERG
EGFR-mutant lung lines (HCC4006 sensitive vs NCIH1650 resistant) show mixed pattern; EGFR signaling may modulate potassium channel dependence
TP53 mutations are common across sensitive lines but also in resistant lines, suggesting weak association
SF3B1 mutations appear in several sensitive lines (HCC95, UO31) but mechanism unclear
CDKN2A loss in sensitive melanoma and other lines may increase proliferation and drug sensitivity
KRAS mutations appear in both sensitive and resistant lines, but some resistant lines (GSU, SNU410) harbor KRAS
NF1 mutations appear in resistant lines (BICR6, S117, FTC133) suggesting possible protection
